correctness.rationale: With L_j=|j+1><j| and L=gamma(J-I), the exact-integral FREE step of Chen et al. is Phi=q I+(1-q) J, q=e^(-gamma tau), whereas the exact channel is e^(x(J-I)). The superoperator J is normal: it cyclically permutes diagonal populations and kills all off-diagonal coherences. Its only fixed matrix is scalar identity. The full Hilbert–Schmidt contraction thus has alpha_n=max(q,sqrt(1-2a_n q(1-q))) and beta_n=e^(-x min(1,a_n)) with a_n=1-cos(2pi/n). Exact n=2,3 factorizations show equality only x<=ln3 or x<=ln2 respectively; for n>=4 the displayed scalar derivative inequality gives strict alpha>beta for all x>0. As q->0, alpha=1-a_n q+O(q^2) and e^(x(J-I))->depolarizing Pi while Phi->J; the maximal density-state trace-norm distance tends 2(1-1/n). Independent finite-dimensional full-superoperator singular-value checks for n=2,3,4,6 corroborate. They do not prove universal dimensions or steps.
